card.name: Abakua
card.tagline: Afro-Cuban men's secret society with masked ireme dancers.
card.profile: Abakua is an all-male Afro-Cuban initiatory religious fraternity founded in 1836 in Regla, derived from the Ekpe ('leopard') societies of the Efik/Efut peoples of the Cross River basin (Calabar). Concentrated in Havana, Matanzas and Cardenas, organized into lodges (potencias). The masked ireme (naango, 'diablito') dancer represents an ancestral spirit, performing sharp, angular, staccato movements echoing the ekue/bonko drums; ceremonies (plantes) involve drumming, dancing and chanting in a secret Abakua language. Public appearances occur on the Day of the Three Kings (6 January) (English Wikipedia; The Appendix).
card.insight: Abakua is considered the only African-origin male initiatory society reconstituted in the Americas, and its rhythms profoundly influenced Cuban popular music, especially the rumba columbia (English Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: Cuba's only masked secret-society dance. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Calabar origin, Cuba.
